checked.label: I’ve been drinking for years. I’m stuck with it.
problems: Vaillant 1996 abstract re-fetched (PubMed 8611061): quote 'After abstinence had been maintained for 5 years, relapse was rare.' is word for word (11 words); quotesMore also word for word.

Figure fits: proof claims only that 5 years off held ('rarely went back'), no more hopeful than 'relapse was rare'. It answers 'stuck' indirectly (getting out lasts) rather than 'most get out'; acceptable since the hero already carries the get-free share and the rule bans repeating it.
Severity disorder and Counted 'men with a drinking problem, mild cases included' (9 words) match: DSM-III alcohol abuse, 205 of 724 men; some were dependent, so 'mild included' is right.
Repeats no figure on the page ('5 years' appears on no card). One idea, 1 figure, plain words. Weak line true (abstract gives no count off 5 years).

Test: 'When this thought comes' step: one small thing at the moment, no trigger sought, no dry-evening or craving-rating drill. 'do the next step of the plan' is safe for a heavy daily drinker because step 1 says don't stop yet. Old test in testR7 and notUsed.beliefs-tests; old proof in wasR7 (notUsed.beliefs per changeNote).

checked.label: I’ve tried to stop before. I always go back.
problems: As the brief says: proof repeats '25 in 100' (card 7 big figure) and restates the how-tries card (Kelly 2019, same table); it carries 3 figures (25, 4, plus 'at least' on a quartile).

Replacement fetched: Witkiewitz & Masyn 2008 (PMC2721008, full text): 563 people in community alcohol treatment (RREP: Providence, Buffalo, Albuquerque; DIS alcohol abuse or dependence); 395 lapsed in the 12 months after; growth-mixture classes after the first lapse: frequent heavy 6%, 'prolapse' 12%, infrequent 82%.

New proof answers 'I always go back' with a different kind of fact (what happens after a slip), 1 figure. '6 in 100' also sits on the after-mood card (42 to 6 in 100) as a different measure; it is the source's own figure, so kept rather than the arithmetic 94 (which also appears in the hero range fold).
Not a moderation proof and must not be read as one: the 82% infrequent group kept drinking; the proof claims only that heavy frequent drinking was rare after a slip. Noted in proofNote.

Test: 'When this thought comes' step: one small thing at the moment, no trigger sought, no dry-evening or craving-rating drill. Sends him to step 3, whose first line is the heavy-drinker doctor pointer, so safe. Two branches (after a slip / when the thought comes).

fix.beliefs[1].proofNote: Witkiewitz & Masyn 2008, RREP: 563 treated for alcohol abuse or dependence (no major psychiatric or more severe drug diagnosis); 395 lapsed within 12 months; after the first lapse, model classes: frequent heavy 6%, frequent then less often 12%, infrequent moderate 82%. The proof claims only the 6; the 82% kept drinking, so it is no case for moderating (belief 5 answers that).
